title: Australian Fires Made 38 Thunderstorms of Their Own in a Week

scenes.text: Australian wildfires made 38 thunderstorms of their own.
In late December 2019 and early January, huge fires created their own storm clouds.
Scientists call them fire thunderstorms. Heat lifts smoke and moist air so high it builds a storm.
Thirty-eight formed in about a week. Twenty of them punched into the stratosphere.
Radar showed their tops above ten miles. The smoke later climbed to nearly 20 miles.
Fires don't just burn. They make weather. Thirty-eight storms, all made by fire.

description:
A study of Australia's Black Summer fires counted 38 fire-driven thunderstorms in about a week, with 20 reaching the stratosphere.
Radar echo tops reached 16.7 km, and the smoke later rose to over 31 km, a record altitude for smoke.
Have you ever seen a storm cloud made by fire?

first_comment: The smoke from those fires circled the planet and stayed in the stratosphere for months. Did you know fires could build their own weather?
